description.narrative: The Goyon Baya Response Project (GBRP) is a locally led multi-sectoral - MPC, WaSH, and Referral Services – 12- month response designed to deliver timely life-saving assistance to the most severely affected, vulnerable, and at-risk target communities in Borno and Katsina States. GBRP will address the acute humanitarian and protection needs of 12,375 highly vulnerable individuals (60% female) or 1,950 households (HHs)] residing in IPC/CH Phase 3+ areas affected by conflict and climate shocks across targeted Wards in Mashi and Ngala LGAs in Katsina and Borno. It will take an integrated, area-based approach through a rapid response mechanism that initiates response within 7 days of an alert, combining MPCA with WaSH, mainly targeting CH/IPC phase 3+ areas that are affected by new shocks and have acute unmet needs. GBRP will prioritize HNRPdesignated communities hosting large numbers of newly affected/displaced households facing severe food insecurity and malnutrition. GBRP also provides a referral mechanism to outside services with links to sectoral coordination working groups, and common donor and government plans, strategies, and common approaches (CWG, OPR, HNRP) in the NW and NE. 80% of funds will be transferred directly to beneficiaries in the MPCA component. The project will be delivered through a localisation-focused consortium which consists of Christian Aid Ireland (CA), a DG ECHO Programmatic Partnership certified and leading Irish INGO on locally led humanitarian and peacebuilding responses, and SHI – a national partner with deep local presence and cash programming expertise operating in NE and NW Nigeria. Strategic links build on SHI’s ongoing ECHO interventions and CA’s implementation of the ECHO-funded Local SPACE (Emergency Response Capacity) project in Borno.
